properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 4 at 7:50PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
Areas of locally dense fog will persist along portions of the
Glenn and Richardson Highways, especially from Glennallen west to
Mendeltna, this evening through early Monday morning.

Periods of a wintry mix of precipitation are also expected across
the Copper River Basin through Monday morning. With temperatures
around freezing for most locations, any precipitation may fall as
a mix of rain, snow, and freezing drizzle. Little to no
significant snow and ice accumulation is expected. However, the
combination of falling precipitation and temperatures around
freezing may result in slippery road conditions and patchy black
ice. The precipitation and fog is expected to taper off by early
to mid Monday morning.

Motorists are urged to slow down and use caution while traveling.
For the latest road conditions call 5 1 1 or visit
511.alaska.gov.

some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the

warmest temperatures will be located in the southern San Joaquin
Valley. Overnight lows between 70 and 75 degrees expected in the
Sierra Foothills where the thermal belt is strongest.

* WHERE...San Joaquin Valley, Sierra Nevada foothills, and Coastal
West Hills.

* WHEN...Until 11 PM PDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures may cause heat illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Moderate to major risk of heat-related
illnesses for much of the population, especially those without
effective cooling or hydration.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.
